name: Vicinity Occlusion Mapping (VOM)
definition: A method utilizing two Summed Area Tables (SATs) computed from a depth map to incorporate view-dependent ambient occlusion and halo effects.
summary: Vicinity Occlusion Mapping is an image-space technique that uses depth-based Summed Area Tables to efficiently compute view-dependent ambient occlusion and halo effects, distinguishing itself by operating on depth maps rather than volumetric density.
